questions.prompt: The finish reason is max-tokens and the reply holds some text and one tool call. What does the assembler return?
options: The text and the tool call, with its arguments as received
The text only; the tool call is dropped
Nothing, because the reply was cut off
The tool call only, since text is less important
questions.explanation: A reply cut off by the output limit may have a tool call whose arguments end mid-JSON. Running it is unsafe, so the assembler keeps the text and drops every tool call.

questions.prompt: Pieces of two tool calls arrive interleaved: index 0, index 1, index 0. How does the assembler keep them apart?
options: It assumes each piece continues the call before it
It waits for the finish chunk and then sorts by arguments
It keys each partial call by the piece's index
It parses each piece as JSON and merges the objects
questions.explanation: Each tool-call-delta carries an index. The assembler keeps one partial call per index and appends each piece's arguments to the right one.

questions.prompt: Why does the loop append the assembled assistant message to the log before running its tool calls?
options: So the log records the exact message the tools follow
Because tools read their arguments from the log file
Because the provider requires it before tools can run
So the tool calls can be edited before they run
questions.explanation: Appending first means the log always holds the message that led to each tool call. If anything goes wrong while tools run, the request behind them is already recorded.
